stories.headline: Ukraine launches ~600-drone barrage on Russia, biggest attack on Moscow in over a year

key_facts.fact: A wave of almost 600 Ukrainian drones attacked Russia overnight, killing four people, including three in the Moscow region and one in Belgorod, with another dozen wounded.
key_facts.excerpt: A wave of almost 600 Ukrainian drones attacked Russia overnight killing four people, authorities said on Sunday, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the barrage an 'entirely justified' retribution for Moscow's own pummelling of Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Russia's defence ministry said air defences shot down 556 drones overnight across the country, with another 30 drones intercepted after dawn; air defences destroyed 81 drones headed for Moscow since midnight, making it the largest attack on the capital in over a year.
key_facts.excerpt: Air defences destroyed 81 drones headed for Moscow since midnight, the Russian news agency TASS reported, citing Mayor Sergei Sobyanin, making it the largest attack on the capital in over a year.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's defence ministry said the strikes hit the Moscow Oil Refinery, the Solnechnogorsk oil depot, and several microelectronics manufacturing facilities for the first time; Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport reported drone debris on its territory.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest attack on Sunday hit 'the Moscow Oil Refinery, the Solnechnogorsk oil depot, and several microelectronics manufacturing facilities for the first time', Ukraine's defence ministry said on social media.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said the SBU and Ukraine's Armed Forces jointly targeted military-industrial and fuel infrastructure in Moscow Oblast and air defense systems at the Belbek military airfield in occupied Crimea, calling the strikes part of a 'shift in the balance' in Kyiv's favor.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's President, Volodymyr Zelensky, praised the Ukrainian military's efforts in delivering 'significant' long-range strikes on Moscow on May 16-17, calling them part of a shift in momentum in Kyiv's favor.

stories.headline: Drone strike sparks fire at UAE's Barakah nuclear plant in 'dangerous escalation'

key_facts.fact: On May 17 the UAE's Defence Ministry said three drones entered the country from the 'western border direction'; two were intercepted while the third struck an electrical generator outside the inner perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Al Dhafra, sparking a fire.
key_facts.excerpt: The country's defence ministry said three drones had entered the UAE from the 'western border direction'. While two were intercepted, the third drone struck an electrical generator 'outside the inner perimeter' of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Abu Dhabi, sparking a fire.

key_facts.fact: The UAE foreign ministry called the strike an 'unacceptable act of aggression' and a 'dangerous escalation'; no injuries were reported and radiological safety levels were unaffected.
key_facts.excerpt: The UAE's foreign ministry called the strike an 'unacceptable act of aggression' and said it had the right to respond to any hostilities. No injuries were reported and there was no impact on radiological safety levels, local authorities said.

key_facts.fact: The IAEA said the strike caused a fire in an electrical generator and one reactor (unit 3) was temporarily powered by emergency diesel generators; director-general Rafael Grossi expressed 'grave concern' and called for 'maximum military restraint'.
key_facts.excerpt: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said Sunday's incident in the UAE forced one reactor to rely temporarily on emergency diesel generators. IAEA chief Rafael Grossi expressed 'grave concern' and warned that military activity threatening nuclear facilities was 'unacceptable'.

key_facts.fact: The $20 billion Barakah plant, built with help from South Korea and online since 2020, is the only nuclear power plant in the Arab world and supplies about a quarter of UAE energy needs; this is the first time the four-reactor complex has been targeted in the war.
key_facts.excerpt: The $20 billion Barakah nuclear power plant was built by the UAE with the help of South Korea and went online in 2020. It is the only nuclear power plant in the Arab world and can provide a quarter of the energy needs in the UAE... It's the first time the four-reactor Barakah plant has been targeted in the war.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia separately said it intercepted three drones from Iraqi airspace the same day; Qatar and Saudi Arabia condemned the UAE attack as a threat to regional stability.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia said [it intercepted three drones] from Iraqi airspace and warned that [it] would take the necessary operational measures to respond to any attempt to violate [its] sovereignty and security.

stories.headline: Trump warns Iran 'better get moving FAST' after national security meeting

key_facts.fact: Trump met with top national security officials on Saturday May 16 at his Virginia golf club to discuss the path forward on the Iran war, then warned Sunday May 17 that Tehran 'better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them'.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump met with top members of his national security team on Saturday to discuss the path forward on the Iran war, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN, a day before he said Tehran 'better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them.'

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, CIA Director John Ratcliffe and special envoy Steve Witkoff attended; the meeting came hours after Trump returned from a visit to China to discuss Iran with Xi Jinping.
key_facts.excerpt: Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, CIA Director John Ratcliffe and special envoy Steve Witkoff all attended the meeting at the president's Virginia golf club, the source said. The gathering occurred just hours after Trump arrived back in Washington from a high-stakes visit to China.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon has prepared a series of military target plans should Trump decide on more strikes, including targeted strikes on energy and infrastructure sites in Iran; Trump is expected to meet again with his national security team early this week.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon has prepared a series of military target plans should Trump ultimately decide to move forward with more strikes, sources familiar with the talks said, including targeted strikes on energy and infrastructure sites in Iran.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan's interior minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other officials, Iranian media said; Pakistan has acted as the primary mediator in US-Iran peace talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian media reported Sunday that Pakistan's interior minister, Mohsin Naqvi, had met with top Iranian officials, including President Masoud Pezeshkian. Pakistan has acted as the primary mediator during the US-Iran peace talks.

stories.headline: 30-year Treasury yield hits 5% as oil rally fuels global bond rout, rate-hike bets surge

key_facts.fact: For the first time in two decades, the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5% as Wall Street priced in greater odds for rate hikes; US, German, Japanese and UK yields all soared while stocks tumbled amid the closed Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Given the fading hopes that energy-fueled inflation will come back down soon, bonds sold off sharply, with U.S., German, Japanese, and U.K. yields all soaring while stocks tumbled. For the first time in two decades, the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5% as Wall Street priced in greater odds for rate hikes.

key_facts.fact: Markets now price a roughly three-in-four chance for a Fed rate hike by December and see a hike as a lock by March, a reversal from late February when two quarter-point cuts were expected for 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Traders now see an interest-rate hike as a lock by March, underscoring how the Iran war has flipped the bond-market narrative on its head since late February, when two quarter-point cuts were expected for 2026. Markets are now suggesting a roughly three-in-four chance for a hike by December.

key_facts.fact: Sunday futures: Dow off 174 points (-0.35%), S&P 500 -0.26%, Nasdaq -0.32%; US oil futures up 1.75% to $107.26/bbl, Brent +1.32% to $110.70; 10-year Treasury yield climbed 1.6 bps to 4.611%.
key_facts.excerpt: Futures tied to the Dow Jones industrial average fell 174 points, or 0.35%. S&P 500 futures were down 0.26%, and Nasdaq futures lost 0.32%. U.S. oil futures rose 1.75% to $107.26 a barrel, while Brent crude climbed 1.32% to $110.70... The yield on the 10-year Treasury climbed 1.6 basis points to 4.611%.

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan predicted commercial oil inventories in the developed world could 'approach operational stress levels' by early June; Capital Economics and UBS warned stockpiles could reach 'critically low levels' by end of June.
key_facts.excerpt: JPMorgan predicted that commercial oil inventories in the developed world could 'approach operational stress levels' by early June. Capital Economics warned oil stockpiles could reach 'critically low levels' by the end of June... UBS also said oil inventories are approaching record lows, warning that 'buffers have now largely been exhausted.'

key_facts.fact: G7 finance chiefs are set to discuss the debt selloff when they meet this week; Wednesday brings the release of the Fed's April meeting minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: Group-of-Seven finance chiefs are set to discuss the debt selloff when they meet this week... This week, investors will focus on Wednesday's release of the Fed's meeting minutes from April, which will reveal the extent to which dissenting voters had support among other officials.

stories.headline: FDA approves Roche's Tecentriq for muscle-invasive bladder cancer guided by ctDNA test

key_facts.fact: On May 17 the FDA approved Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza as adjuvant treatment for adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who have circulating tumor DNA molecular residual disease (ctDNA MRD) after cystectomy, identified by Natera's Signatera CDx assay.
key_facts.excerpt: Genentech, a member of the Roche Group... announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Tecentriq® (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza® (atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs) as an adjuvant treatment for adult patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who have circulating tumor DNA molecular residual disease (ctDNA MRD) after cystectomy, as identified by Natera's Signatera™ CDx personalized MRD assay.

key_facts.fact: Approval was based on Phase III IMvigor011, which showed Tecentriq cut the risk of disease recurrence or death (DFS) by 36% and the risk of death (OS) by 41% in patients with detectable ctDNA MRD identified via serial testing within one year of cystectomy.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA decision was based on positive results from the Phase III IMvigor011 study, which showed that Tecentriq reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death (DFS) by 36% and the risk of death (OS) by 41% in patients with detectable ctDNA MRD identified via serial testing within one year of cystectomy.

key_facts.fact: IMvigor011 is the first prospective Phase III study to show that a ctDNA-guided approach to adjuvant therapy can significantly improve survival in muscle-invasive bladder cancer; the safety profile was generally consistent with prior studies.
key_facts.excerpt: The safety profile was generally consistent with previous studies of Tecentriq. IMvigor011 is the first prospective Phase III study to demonstrate that a ctDNA-guided approach to adjuvant therapy can significantly improve survival in MIBC.

sources.title: FDA Approves Genentech's Tecentriq for Adjuvant Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer With ctDNA-Guided Treatment

stories.headline: FDA approves AstraZeneca-Daiichi Enhertu for two HER2+ early breast cancer indications

key_facts.fact: On May 17 the FDA approved Enhertu (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) for two new HER2-positive early breast cancer indications, covering neoadjuvant (pre-surgery) use based on DESTINY-Breast11 and adjuvant (post-surgery) use based on DESTINY-Breast05.
key_facts.excerpt: Enhertu® (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) has been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for two new breast cancer indications in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings of patients with HER2 positive early breast cancer.

key_facts.fact: In DESTINY-Breast05, Enhertu cut the risk of invasive disease recurrence or death by 53% versus T-DM1 in patients with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy (HR=0.47; 95% CI 0.34–0.66; p<0.0001); three-year IDFS was 92.4% vs 83.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: In DESTINY-Breast05, Enhertu significantly reduced the risk of invasive disease recurrence or death (invasive disease-free survival [IDFS]) by 53% (hazard ratio [HR]=0.47; 95% CI: 0.34-0.66; p<0.0001) compared to trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)... Enhertu demonstrated a three-year IDFS rate of 92.4% (95% CI: 89.7-94.4) and 83.7% with T-DM1.

key_facts.fact: Enhertu is now approved for nine indications, six across both early and metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, marking its expansion into the curative-intent setting for AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo.
key_facts.excerpt: Enhertu now approved for nine indications with six across both early and metastatic HER2 positive breast cancer... Two new indications bring Daiichi Sankyo and AstraZeneca's Enhertu into curative-intent setting, reinforcing its role across stages of HER2 positive breast cancer.

sources.title: Enhertu Approved in the U.S. for Two New Indications for Patients with HER2 Positive Early Breast Cancer
Enhertu approved in two HER2+ early BC settings

stories.headline: SpaceX Dragon CRS-34 docks at ISS with 6,500 lbs of cargo and new science experiments

key_facts.fact: At 6:37 a.m. EDT on May 17, the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft docked autonomously to the forward port of the ISS Harmony module on the 34th SpaceX commercial resupply mission for NASA, carrying nearly 6,500 pounds of food, supplies and equipment for Expedition 74.
key_facts.excerpt: At 6:37 a.m. EDT, the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft docked to the forward port of the International Space Station's Harmony module, carrying nearly 6,500 pounds of food, supplies, and equipment for the Expedition 74 crew. This is the 34th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission to the space station for NASA.

key_facts.fact: Cargo included a new instrument to study charged particles around Earth that can impact power grids and satellites, a bone scaffold made from wood that could enable treatments for osteoporosis, and equipment to evaluate how red blood cells and the spleen change in space.
key_facts.excerpt: Dragon will deliver several new experiments, including a project to determine how well Earth-based simulators mimic microgravity conditions, a bone scaffold made from wood that could produce new treatments for fragile bone conditions like osteoporosis, and equipment to help researchers evaluate how red blood cells and the spleen change in space.

key_facts.fact: Six spaceships are now parked at the station, including CRS-34 Dragon, Crew-12 Dragon, Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL, the Soyuz MS-28 crew ship, and Progress 94 and 95 resupply ships; Dragon will remain docked about a month before splashdown in the Pacific.
key_facts.excerpt: Six spaceships are parked at the space station including the SpaceX CRS-34 Dragon, the SpaceX Crew-12 Dragon, Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL, the Soyuz MS-28 crew ship, and the Progress 94 and 95 resupply ships.
